title: Breakfast Before Class
transcript: When a college began serving free breakfast, the organizers counted each meal and thought the turnout looked encouraging. They soon realized that many customers were students who already ate breakfast regularly. To learn who was missing out, they asked students in early classes about their morning routines. A common problem was that the dining hall opened after the first shuttle from student housing arrived. The college tried handing out simple breakfast bags beside the shuttle stop before lectures. A follow-up survey found that fewer students in those early classes reported skipping breakfast, although the college had yet to measure changes in attendance.

questions.prompt: Why did organizers look beyond the number of meals served?
options: Some students took several meals at once.
The meal count varied with the class schedule.
Many customers already had a habit of eating breakfast.
Dining hall staff had counted students from other colleges.
questions.answer: Many customers already had a habit of eating breakfast.
questions.explanation: 许多来领餐的学生原本就常吃早餐，因此餐数无法说明项目是否覆盖了常常不吃早餐的人。

questions.prompt: What conclusion did the follow-up survey support?
options: More students attended their early classes.
Skipping breakfast became less common among students in early classes.
Students who ate breakfast regularly switched to later classes.
Fewer students needed to take the first shuttle.
questions.answer: Skipping breakfast became less common among students in early classes.
questions.explanation: 后续调查显示，上早课的学生中自报不吃早餐的人减少了。
